subject: OrchidAI: GPU surge readiness & temporary hold request
messages:
From: Evan Torres <evan@orchid.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-04T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Capacity ask — expansion pilot needs / short-term hold?

Hi Mina,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team at OrchidAI is excited to proceed to a late-stage pilot that could convert to a committed Dedicated plan. Before we lock timelines, we need visibility on GPU availability for a 6–8 week pilot window starting mid-May.

Quick summary of their ask (attached):
- Peak concurrent workers: 12 (max prompt length ~4k tokens)
- Preferred instance: A100-40GB or equivalent quantized variant
- Expected sustained throughput: ~600 tokens/sec aggregate
- Pilot start target: week of 2027-05-17

Two asks from our side:
1) Can Redwood perform an availability check and give a sizing recommendation + rough per-hour estimate?
2) If inventory is tight, can we put a short-term "soft hold" on the required capacity so OrchidAI has priority while they complete procurement?

Attaching a short CSV with the target configuration and an updated growth profile. If it helps, Janelle (cc'd) can jump on a quick call to walk through the workload characteristics.

Thanks — Evan

Attachments: orchid_must-have_gpus.csv, orchid_growth_profile_v2.xlsx, NDA_Orchid_signed.pdf

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Evan Torres <evan@orchid.ai>, Janelle Park <janelle.park@orchid.ai>
Date: 2027-04-04T10:01:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Capacity ask — expansion pilot needs / short-term hold?

Team — forwarding Orchid's request. TL;DR: late-stage pilot (ORCH-4721) wants ~12 concurrent A100-sized workers for ~6–8 weeks starting ~May 17. They asked for a sizing + availability check and, if needed, a short-term priority hold.

Please respond with:
- Quick sizing confirmation (we can give a recommended config that balances latency and cost)
- Inventory availability across US regions for the May window
- Whether Sales Ops can create a "soft hold" ticket and how long we can keep it without disrupting other commitments

Related HubSpot: https://hubspot.redwood/deal/ORCH-4721
I attached the CSV they sent for reference.

Mina
Director, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-04T11:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity ask — expansion pilot needs / short-term hold?

Mina / team — did a quick run of current and projected allocation for mid-May. Notes below are conservative and assume normal churn (no emergency decommissions).

Inventory snapshot (US regions, as of 2027-04-04):
- A100-40GB equiv (bare metal / dedicated pool): 48 units total, of which 32 are unallocated.
- H100/80GB quantized equivalents: 16 units unallocated (better perf per watt but require model validation).
- Buffer reserved for committed enterprise: 8 units (can be negotiated if approvals come through).

Sizing recommendation for OrchidAI pilot:
- Start: 8 workers A100-40GB + 4 workers on quantized H100-equivalents (fallback mix)
- Rationale: gives headroom for the peak concurrency while keeping cost reasonable; can autoscale to +4 workers if sustained load increases.
- Expected inference cost (rough): $X/hour per A100 worker, $Y/hour per quantized worker (I will put exact numbers into the pricing worksheet by EOD).

Soft-hold feasibility:
- We can place a 21-calendar-day soft hold on up to 16 units with Sales Ops flagging them as "priority prospect: ORCH-4721". It won't remove them from inventory but will prevent automatic hard allocation to new Dedicated contracts without a manual override.
- Longer holds (30+ days) need approval from Capacity Planning (Marcus) + Finance for opportunity cost.

Next steps: I will update the pricing worksheet + attach per-hour estimates. If Harrison (capacity) asks, point them to this thread and the HubSpot deal.

- Dev
Lead, Infrastructure Planning

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-04T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity ask — expansion pilot needs / short-term hold?

Thanks Dev — +1 on the 8 + 4 split as a default. Operational items from Capacity Planning's side: 

- Can sales accept a 21-day soft hold? That window is reasonable operationally and preserves our ability to reassign if a firm committed contract hits a hard SLA.
- Impact: If we approve the 21-day soft hold for 16 units, we will need to flag any other late-stage deals (we have two other prospects in Q2 asking for 10+ units each) and coordinate rollbacks or prioritize by signed commitment date.
- Fallback: Recommend we offer Orchid a "priority queue" (soft hold) + canary burst option: if usage exceeds the soft hold, route to burst-capacity pool (higher price) so we avoid throttling existing committed customers.

I'll prepare a short Ops note that outlines which deals are impacted and proposed prioritization. Ping me if you want the note within the hour.

Marcus
Senior Manager, Capacity Planning

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Evan Torres <evan@orchid.ai>, Janelle Park <janelle.park@orchid.ai>
Date: 2027-04-05T15:43:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Capacity ask — expansion pilot needs / short-term hold?

Team — after reviewing Dev and Marcus's notes, I'm authorizing a 21-calendar-day soft hold for up to 16 units (ORCH-4721). Sales Ops, please create "SOFTHOLD-ORCH-4721" ticket and tag capacity:orchid-priority. Finance: expect a heads-up; we'll hold pricing at the quoted preliminary rates until procurement completes.

Action items:
- Sales Ops (assigned): create soft-hold ticket, add note to HubSpot (https://hubspot.redwood/deal/ORCH-4721), and attach the Orchid CSV.
- Dev: finalize per-hour estimates and drop into the HubSpot quote doc.
- Marcus: publish the short Ops note listing other Q2 late-stage asks and the prioritization rule (signed-commitment date -> priority).
- Mina: coordinate a 30-min sync with Orchid next week to confirm procurement timeline.

I'll approve extending the hold beyond 21 days only after Finance signs off on the opportunity cost memo.

Thanks — Laura
Head of Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
